spans.s:
nítya, a.
 —1. own (Vedic), 79^16;
 —2. constant;
 eternal, 57^7; -am, adv. constantly,
always, 17^16, 64^19. [in mg 1, fr. ni, ‘in,’
1245b, and so signifying ‘inward, not
alien.’]

nitya-kāla, m. uninterrupted time; -am,
adv. always, under all circumstances, 60^6.

nitya-snāyin, a. constantly making
sacred ablutions. [1279.]

nīti, f.
 —1. cónduct, esp. right and sagacious
conduct; the knowledge of all that
governs virtuous and discreet and statesman-like
behavior; political and social
ethics;
 —2. leading. [√nī, ‘condúct.’]

nīti-jñá, a. knowing how to conduct
one's self discreetly.

nīti-vidyā, f. knowledge of nīti or
political and social ethics, esp. as it concerns
princes.

nīti-śāstra, n. doctrine or science of
political and social ethics.
